title: 120/240 V split-phase utility service, 25 kVA transformer

sources.citation: A single-phase overhead (pole-mounted) distribution transformer serving a house: 25 kVA is a common size for one to a few homes, with an impedance of about 1.5–3 % and an X/R ratio of about 1–3, typical of published manufacturers' data and utility service guides for small single-phase units (paraphrased, not one vendor's). 2 % and an X/R of 2 are taken: a full-winding impedance of 0.02 × 240² / 25 000 = 46.1 mΩ, about 5.2 kA of bolted fault current across L1–L2, the infinite-primary (transformer-limited) available fault current: an upper bound, with no utility system impedance.
120 V from each line to the neutral (the secondary's centre tap), the 120/240 V single-phase three-wire nominal system of ANSI C84.1-2020 (the region profile's split-phase system).
game-design: a placeholder size and terminal layout. The service is headless in P2 (no service entrance or meter base until P4), so it is not drawn.

game-design: in P3 this service is the stand-in supply of the demo circuit (D12), standing in for P4's load centre, so its terminals take a branch circuit the way a 15 A breaker's and a neutral bar's do: one 14 to 10 AWG copper or aluminium conductor each, solid or stranded, a 13 ± 2 mm strip and a 4.0 N·m marked torque (the values of the breaker-terminal class in breaker.saltmere-1p-15a). Conductors enter at the terminals and leave along +z. Not a transformer secondary's real terminals; P4 replaces it.
